newsitem.title: YEMEN: Leading candidates in Yemeni polls.
newsitem.headline: Leading candidates in Yemeni polls.

text.p: Yemen on Sunday will hold its first parliamentary elections since a 1994 civil war nearly tore the impoverished Arab state apart.
Some 2,306 candidates, including 17 women, are seeking 301 seats in the chamber from 12 parties or as independents.
The main opposition Yemen Socialist Party (YSP) and three others have announced they will boycott the polls in protest at alleged irregularities.
Remaining contenders include merchants, tribal leaders, doctors, engineers and the speaker of parliament.

PRESIDENT ALI ABDULLAH SALEH's job will not be contested in the general elections. Saleh, who has led the north since 1978 and ruled unified Yemen since the north and south merged in 1990, will seek re-election in a separate poll next year.

AHMED MOHAMMAD Al-ANSI is a leading contender for the ruling General People's Congress (GPC), a wide grouping of supporters of President Saleh. Al-Ansi, communications minister and member of parliament, has gained popularity by pushing for telecommunications projects in Yemen.

The GPC will head to the polls with a familiar name, AHMED ALI SALEH, the 27-year-old son of the president. It is his first appearance in Yemen's political arena. Aside from the weight of his name, Ahmed has also been launching charity drives.

The Islamist Yemeni Islah Party's (YIP) best hope is parliamentary speaker SHEIKH ABDULLAH BIN HUSSEIN AL-AHMAR, a charismatic figure who enjoys wide tribal backing. Al-Ahmar is renowned for his skills as a mediator between the government and tribes during times of crisis. Islah, junior partner in the coalition with GPC, is pushing for a wider application of Islamic law.

SULTAN HEZAM AL-A'TWANI is member of parliament for the opposition Nasserite Unionist Popular Organisation. The owner of a Sanaa bookshop, he is a leading opposition figure in the outgoing parliament. He was the only candidate from his party to win a seat in the 1993 general elections.

ABDEL WAHAB MAHMOUD, one of the founders of the opposition Arab Socialist Baa'th Party in Yemen and a former minister of supply and trade, is expected to help the party maintain a foothold in the chamber.
